description: In Malesia the leaves are used as a paste against itches, eaten against syphilis, and a decoction is drunk after childbirth. In Jana the leaves are used against mumps, rheumatism, pimples, and piles; a decoction of the flowers is also used against cough and thrush. The fruits are eaten fresh or pickled, but are more acid than those of the preceding species. The juice is generally used against fever, scurvy, beri-beri, biliousness, coughs, and piles; it also removes stains from laundry, hands, and weapons.
